xpp.mmu: Unicorn ARMv7-A CPU page-table walker; guest CP15 and page tables

gic.basis: Kernel CBAR reads and GIC distributor/CPU-interface accesses at CBAR+0x1000/+0x2000. CBAR 0xffff0000 is a declared discovery input, not captured.

interval_timer.clock: one timer cycle per aggregate CPU instruction; synthetic ratio, not measured
interval_timer.basis: Control +0 is written with an inverted select mask, per-channel configuration at +0x10+n*4, count and reload at +0x100+n*0x10; one channel is read as a running counter. Channel n raises interrupt 48+n: the X-T20 2.11 timer library (0xc4bcd0) maps channel n through byte table 0xed3b58 to row n+2 of interrupt descriptor table 0xed4720, whose first word is 0x30+n.

flash_controller.basis: Flash reads go through the aperture at 0xf0000000+offset by CPU copies and DMA; the controller's configuration words are written around each copy. Commands: +0x00 opcode, +0x04 aperture address, +0x10 control (chip select in bits 6-7), +0x20 phase count, +0x1c start; +0x24 status and +0x28 mask, where a set mask bit also acknowledges its status. Page programs are aperture stores while the registers hold opcode 0x12, ended by +0x30 bit 0. X-T20 2.11 driver 0xc5182c/0xc5220c; its handler 0xc501c0 is connected through descriptor 0xed4804, interrupt 0x23.

pl330.timing: 16 guest setup ticks plus ceil(bytes/16); functional transfer timing reused from XP4, not measured bus bandwidth.
pl330.basis: Channel programs start through DMAGO written to the debug instruction registers; the driver's IRQ table maps event n to line 207+n.

serial_ports.basis: Declared discovery input: a provisional status law without a peer. Sends complete at once and set done bit 2, writes to +0x2c clear status bits, bit 3 reads set and received words read zero. The attached peers are not identified.

decompressor.basis: Method-4 streaming decompressor with the XP4 register interface: the X-T20 2.11 section-6 loader resets it through +0 (0xc5d584), waits for +0 to read nonzero and for +0x24 to read 0x10001, and connects interrupt descriptor row 0x12 of 0xed4720 (interrupt 0x81) with handler 0xc5d348 (0xc5d440).

dmp.basis: DMP SMAPH vector-graphics renderer with the XP4 register interface. The X-T20 2.11 OpenVG/EGL driver (seg5 0xdda65c onward, kernel tasks smaphk/smaphp) programs command words at +0x1c, the copy unit at +0xc00-+0xc18 (initialization 0xdda748 sets +0xc1c to 0x8000) and command lists at +0x10d0/+0x10e0. Its interrupt 92 handler 0xdda2fc reads status +0x34, and waiter 0xdda3cc reports bits 31, 30 and 26.

adc.basis: Twelve-channel ADC with the X-T20 2.11 kernel contract (0x5ac00..0x5adf8): control +0 with start bit 0, continuous-mode bit 1 and channel enables in bits 16-25, clock divider +4, and 10-bit results at +0x10 + 4*channel. Reader 0x5ad8c requires bit 0 and the channel enable; a single conversion clears bit 0 when done (stage 2 0x13d8 waits for it). The conversion clock is unmeasured; sample_ticks is a declared input.

display_frames.basis: Frame interrupts of the display controller, as an interrupt law without its registers. Seg5 source table 0xed4720 rows 73-78 connect lines 112-114 and 117-119 (edge) to handlers that run the callbacks queued by 0xc9dc38 for output 0 or 1 and event 0-2 (0xc9d854, 0xc9d994); the handlers read no controller register. The X-T20 2.11 vglib thread clears bit 16 of 0xfff65000 or 0xfff5a000, queues such a callback and yields at priority 7 until it runs (0xcad290), which starves flashload before section 7 loads. The period is an assumed 60 Hz in 48 MHz timer ticks (the 10 ms system tick reloads 480000); the panel rate is not measured.

gpio.basis: Sixteen GPIO banks with a 0x40 stride and input levels at +0x14, the same layout as the XP4 banks: X-T20 2.11 stage 2 (0x102c) copies the sixteen input words into the boot information and seg5 0xc4e138 reads the live register. Discovery up to REC writes only registers 0-7 of each bank.

pll_clocks.basis: Clock bank of X-T20 2.11 section 5: table 0xed5538 lists five PLLs as (configuration, configuration, control, lock bit) = (+0x28, +0x2c, +0x30, 2), (+0x34, +0x38, +0x3c, 4), (+0x40, +0x44, +0x48, 16), (+0x4c, +0x50, +0x54, 8), (+0x78, +0x7c, +0x80, 1); 0xc6aa74 sets control bit 26 and polls +0x6c for the lock bit, 0xc6aa30 clears bit 26. +0x58..+0x64 hold paired 12-bit divider fields (0xc6ae68) and 0xc6a6e0 polls divider busy bits at +0x68, which read clear. The lock time is an assumed 100 us in 48 MHz ticks; it is not measured.

imaging_control.basis: Imaging control page of X-T20 2.11 section 5: +0x000 bit 0 is a run bit that 0xc33ec8 clears and then waits to read set (stopped); six register-bus channels at +0x200 + 0x40*n (0xc345b4..0xc34c50) send a RAM frame 0x81 hi lo value (write) or 0x82 hi lo (read) to a select in configuration bits 8-12 and return the reply byte in bits 15:8 of eight receive words at +0x1c. The imaging-side chip is a register file: the start-up writes a register and reads it back until it matches (seg6 0x17fa434). Commands and stops complete at once; what the chip does with the values is not modeled.

imaging_statistics.basis: Imaging statistics engine of X-T20 2.11 section 5: configuration and output buffer words +0x04..+0x1e4, interrupt enables in the low ten bits of +0x04 and start bit 28 of +0x1e8. Descriptor row 0x32 connects it to interrupt 106 (level); handler 0xc36280 reads the status +0x08 and writes it back to clear it. The stop sequence 0xc365a8 clears +0x00 bit 0, waits until +0x00 reads 1 and +0x1ec bit 16 (idle) reads set, then clears the start bit; 0xc398c4 waits for the same idle bit. While started, the model finishes a frame at every frame-sync tick and reports every enabled status bit, so a frame is never in flight; the statistics are not computed and the buffers are not written. Without these completions, REC re-entry after a USB session stops in imgdc job 0x26 (observed in an independent X-T20 emulator).

hdmi_tx.basis: Synopsys DesignWare HDMI TX controller of X-T20 2.11 section 5, byte registers at a four-byte stride (generated accessors 0xcb29xx..0xcb8xxx): IH_FC_STAT0.. at +0x400, IH_MUTE_FC_STAT0.. at +0x600, IH_MUTE at +0x7fc (0xcb3c98), FC_DBGFORCE/FC_DBGTMDS0-2 at +0x4800/+0x4864..+0x486c and PHY_CONF0..PHY_POL0 at +0xc000..+0xc01c. 0xcbe578 reads PHY_STAT0 (+0xc010, 0xcb7df8) and takes bit 1 as hot plug and bits 4-7 as receiver sense; 0xcbe5e0 starts the connection only on hot plug. No HDMI cable was attached during the reference captures, so the controller is an idle law: PHY_STAT0 and the interrupt status registers read 0 and the other used registers read back.

frame_sync.basis: Imaging frame sync of X-T20 2.11 section 5. 0xc3fd10..0xc401b4 program the timing words +0x04..+0x58; +0x00 takes bit 1 from 0xc3fc98, bits 0, 1 and 4 from 0xc3fcb8 and loses bit 1 in 0xc3fce0, and seg6 0x16b91bc clears bit 0 and waits until it reads set while bit 1 may be clear, so bit 0 is a frame flag set every frame from tick zero; the other bits read back, and whether they gate the frames is not known. The frame interrupt words are imaging control +0x140 (enable, written by 0xc35a08) and +0x144 (status, write 1 to clear, 0xc359b4) with bits 0, 8 and 16. 0xd09dc8 connects frame source n to descriptor row byte 0xf67188 + 3n and handler word 0xf64858 + 4n: source 0 is row 0x2a (interrupt 100, level) with handler 0xd099ec, which clears status bit 8; source 1 is row 0x2c (interrupt 102, edge) with handler 0xd09958, which clears bit 0. Row 0x2b (interrupt 101, bit 16) has no handler word and is not modeled. Without interrupt 102 the recording start-up never receives completion 0x11cd; without 100, REC re-entry after a USB session stops after step 0x02010200 (observed in an independent X-T20 emulator). Both sources latch on the same frame tick; the phase between them is not known. The period is an assumed 60 Hz in 48 MHz timer ticks; what the timing words select is not modeled.

reset_gates.basis: Reset and gate controls of X-T20 2.11 section 5. SD start-up 0xc65b18 drives +0x1c bit 18, 19 or 20 low and then high for SD channel 0, 1 or 2 and then sets bit 0; the UHS-II fallback at 0xc65dc4 repeats it before rewriting the host power and clock words by read-modify-write, so a falling edge resets that SD host. 0xc65a04/0xc65e58 set and clear +0x14 bit 22 around the UHS-II attempt and 0xc621d0/0xc620b8 set and clear pad bits in +0x70 and +0x88; +0x08, +0x20 and +0x6c are read-modify-written by 0xc621a0, 0xc694fc, 0xcc0590 and 0xc65c7c. Words read back their last write; what the gate bits switch is not modeled.

dram_controller.basis: DRAM controller of X-T20 2.11 section 5. 0xc8f09c reads the refresh-rate level from bits 8..10 of +0xec (caching it at 0xfdbea8 + 5) and, when it changes, rewrites the low half of the refresh words +0x9c and +0xa0 through 0xc8f044: 0xc30 below level 4, 0x618 at level 4; above level 4 it reports event 0x8015. A second controller at 0xfff0f000 is used only when 0xfda438 is set, which it is not in the s1-s3 captures. The boot code that programs the controller before the kernel is not modeled.

xpp_i2c.basis: DesignWare APB I2C masters of X-T20 2.11 section 5: transfer 0xc52b30, API 0xc5328c and interrupt handler 0xc52df8 (bus entries 0xc53264/0xc53278). Bus n is at 0xfff1f000 + 0x1000*n; interrupt descriptor rows 0x50/0x51 of table 0xed471c connect buses 0/1 to interrupts 68/69. Each transfer disables the bus, writes SCL counts 0x533/0x545 (standard) and 0x13f/0x151 (fast), IC_CON speed and restart enable, IC_TAR, the 0x5f interrupt mask and zero FIFO thresholds, then enables it; the handler feeds DATA_CMD on TX_EMPTY while IC_STATUS.TFNF is set, with STOP on the last byte and RESTART on the first read of a write-then-read, drains it on RX_FULL and ends on TX_ABRT, and the task then polls IC_STATUS.MST_ACTIVITY. The interrupt mask is written before IC_ENABLE, so TX_EMPTY is taken as asserted only while enabled. An ic_clk of 266 MHz is inferred from the standard-mode counts giving a symmetric 5 us/5 us 100 kHz clock; it is not measured. The FIFO depth is declared, not measured. Ticks are the 48 MHz timer ticks.

xpp_sd.basis: SD channel 0 of X-T20 2.11 section 5 (0xc6164c..0xc65f24): channel n is at 0xfff92000 + 0x1000*n with its SDHCI bank at +0x200 for channel 0 and +0x100 otherwise. 0xc6592c..0xc65a48 program vendor words +0x20, +0x24 and +0xec; 0xc658cc then tries the UHS-II interface (VDD2 power, host control 2 = 0x107, internal clock) and 0xc65d90 reads present-state bit 31, which is clear for a card without UHS-II, so the driver resets the host through the reset gates and starts the 3.3 V interface. Interrupt descriptor row 0x19 of table 0xed471c connects channel 0 to interrupt 83 (rows 0x1a/0x1b: channels 1/2, 84/85). Clock settle (1 us), transfer (100 us) and wrapper reset (1 us) times are assumed, not measured.

display_outputs.basis: Output 1 of the display controller, 0xfff64000-0xfff67000, as word registers that read back their last write. Two status laws from X-T20 2.11 seg5: 0xca37ac saves +0, writes bit 16, clears it and polls until bit 16 reads set before restoring the saved word with bit 16; 0xca9df0 sets bit 28 of +0x2000 and polls until it reads clear. Both requests complete at once; the controller's real latency (likely one frame) is not measured. Output 0 at 0xfff59000 follows the same bit-16 law in 0xca37ac but is not exercised up to REC and is not declared.

limits: Two cores are a declared discovery input from a public dual Cortex-A7 listing; the count is not measured.
Storage covers the flash aperture, PL330 memory-to-memory programs and the method-4 decompressor. The DMP renderer and display output 1 registers are declared; no pixels are scanned out.
No boot ROM, reset-release controller or external peripheral replies are assumed.
xpp.cache_basis: Declared discovery input: the XP4 Cortex-A7 capacities, unmeasured. Not a cache timing model.
